result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.delete_edges_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Delete all selected edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1014-L1085){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.delete_edges_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Removes edges in the current selection from the graph. Node connectivity may be affected, but nodes themselves remain in the graph. Updates selection state automatically. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This operates on the current edge selection. Deleting the two middle edges of a five-node path leaves every node in place, since removing edges never removes nodes: ::: {#ec5cc4b5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) # path: 0-1-2-3-4 edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids()[1:3] graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids) graph.delete_edges_ws() graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: Only the two selected edges are removed, so the first and last edges of the path still connect their endpoints: ::: {#0df2719c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids()[1:3] graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids) graph.delete_edges_ws() graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Selecting edges by predicate makes it easy to prune a graph based on edge attributes, such as removing low-weight connections: ::: {#3e98a3c3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=5.0) .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=2.0) ) graph.select_edges(lambda e: e.weight and e.weight < 2.0) graph.delete_edges_ws() # only the two edges with weight >= 2.0 remain graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
